title: Exactly One Edit Apart
statement:
You get two strings s and t. An edit is one of: insert one character anywhere, delete one character, or replace one character with a different one.

Return true if s can be turned into t with exactly one edit. Two equal strings are zero edits apart, so they give false.

examples.why: Replace the r with an s.
Insert a p at the front. Comparing position by position would see five mismatches; you have to line the strings up around the edit.
Swapping two letters takes two replacements.

constraints: s and t contain lowercase letters
hints: If the lengths differ by two or more, no single edit can fix that. What are the only length differences left?
Walk both strings until the first position where they differ. Before it, everything matches. What must be true about the rest?

At the first mismatch: with equal lengths, the tails after it must be equal (a replacement). With lengths differing by one, the longer string's tail after it must equal the shorter string's tail from it (an insertion). If there is no mismatch, the answer is true only when the lengths differ by one.

explain.intuition:
One edit only touches one place. So both strings agree on everything before that place, and after it they agree again, just shifted by one if the edit was an insert or delete. Find the first mismatch and you have found where the edit must be, so a single comparison of the remaining tails settles it.

Swap the strings so s is never the longer one. Then there are only two cases: same length, where the edit is a replacement, or t one longer, where it is an insertion into s. A deletion is just the same insertion seen from the other side.
steps: If s is longer than t, swap them. If t.length − s.length > 1, return false.
Find the first index i where s[i] ≠ t[i].
Same length: return whether s from i + 1 equals t from i + 1.
t one longer: return whether s from i equals t from i + 1.
No mismatch at all: return whether t is exactly one longer (its extra character is at the end).
pitfalls: Returning true for two equal strings. Zero edits is not one edit.
Counting mismatches position by position when the lengths differ. An insert near the front shifts every later character.
Forgetting the case where the strings match until the shorter one ends, like "xyz" and "xyzz".

complexity.space: O(1) with index loops (slicing costs O(n) extra)

solutions.title: Try every possible edit spot
solutions.idea: For equal lengths count mismatches. Otherwise delete each character of the longer string in turn and compare with the shorter.

solutions.title: Jump to the first mismatch
solutions.idea: Make s the shorter string. At the first mismatch, the edit is decided; compare what is left in one pass.

followups: Return true if the strings are at most k edits apart. What does the general solution look like, and can you limit it to a band around the diagonal?
Check a word against a whole dictionary for words one edit away. How would you avoid comparing against every word?
